     3	are not shown a question that closed the day before. Driven through `replay.run` as the replay script calls it; no item, so no

1	# Closing due questions in the new system's daily loop: design for the council (round 22), 2026-11-16, $0
     2	
     3	**Goal (gate 5, D548: integration).** The new system's store is read by production's page and closed by production's closing
     4	step (`pull.end_of_day`; D54, D356: at the end of a day passed in, every open question whose due day has come is frozen at its
     5	last answer, or closed "no data to verify" if never judged). The copy check (`INTEGRATION-CHECK.md`) showed the closing works on a
     6	new-system store; the new loop does not call it and instead refuses to run past a due day (`ladder_adapter.LadderAdapter.due_day_guard`).
     7	One owner: the closing rule stays in `pull.py`; the new loop calls it in production's order (`replay.py`: the day's items, the
     8	day's judging round, `pull.end_of_day`, `complete_day`). Nothing frozen changes (the base adapter, Step 1, Step 2, the ladder
     9	step, the judge); only `clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/stage_b/ladder_adapter.py`.
    10	
    11	**Found on the way, fixed in production's own loop (same slice, AGENTS §1):** on a day without items, a closing takes its own
    12	sequence, but `replay.py` completed the day at the sequence before it, so the next day's items were shown the closed question as
    13	open (`views_open_at_day_start`). Census: 5 closings by the closing step in 139 stored stores, none on a day without items (0 of
    14	5). Fix: the day is completed at the last sequence it wrote (`store.next_sequence(conn) - 1` after the closing). Test
    15	`tests/test_closing_on_a_day_without_items.py` through `replay.run` failed on the old line at its decisive assertion and passes;
    16	`test_pull`, `test_sequential_replay`, `test_no_seed_replay` pass.
    17	
    18	## 1. State × event (the new loop, after the change)
    19	
    20	| State of a question \ event | A day with articles | A day without articles | Its due day | A link from Step 1's trace or the later-linking log | Run ends | Crash mid-day |
    21	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
    22	| Open, never judged | links written; judged in the day's round if changed | nothing; day completed | judged that day if changed, then closed at the day's end ("no data to verify" if still never judged) | written, the question queued for the round | stays open | the judge store is new each run and not resumed (unchanged) |
    23	| Open, judged | as above | nothing; day completed | judged if changed, then frozen at its last answer | written, queued | stays open | as above |
    24	| Opened already due (due day on or before its opening day) | opened, linked, judged if changed, closed at that day's end (production's order) | (not opened on a day without articles) | same day | written that day | closed | as above |
    25	| Closed | **not linked**: the link is dropped and counted with its reason "question closed" (production never shows a closed question to its reading step, so it never links one) | nothing | (not closed again: `pull.end_of_day` closes only open questions) | dropped and counted | closed | as above |
    26	| A theme closed | its open dependants are judged by production's round, which leaves closed themes out of the theme block (`judging.py`) | — | — | dropped and counted | — | — |
    27	
    28	**Days.** The loop walks every calendar day from the first article's day to the run's end day (the last article's day unless an
    29	end day is passed), as production does; a day without articles has no article work and no judging (nothing changed), then the
    30	closing and the day's completion. **The guard** becomes an invariant: at a day's start no open question is due before that day
    31	(the closings of every earlier day ran); a breach refuses the run (it can only come from a store this loop did not write).
    32	
    33	## 2. Value × reader
    34	
    35	| Value written | Readers (searched) | Effect |
    36	|---|---|---|
    37	| `view_switches` closed rows (`pull.close_view`) | `service.is_open_as_of`, `service.views`, `bundle`, `judging.round_of_judgements` (closed left out), `store.views_open_at_day_start` (production's reading step only), `pull.end_of_day` (no second closing) | the page shows the question closed from its due day; no later judging |
    38	| the closing's processing record on a day without articles (`pull.closing_sequence`) | `service.seq_day_map`, `store.next_sequence` | the closing is dated on its day |
    39	| `days_completed` for every calendar day, at the last sequence written | `service.default_as_of`, `bundle`, `store.day_start_seq` | the page's default day is the run's last day, not the last article day |
    40	| the dropped links' count | the run's counts (`run.json`) | read by the run's reader; nothing else |
    41	
    42	## 3. New path × old checks
    43	
    44	- `leakage_check(day, seq)`: unchanged; it reads views, evidence, sources, links, same claims and revisions, none of which the
    45	  closing writes.
    46	- The extension proof's 19 checks: a replay ending before any due day writes the same requests and judgements; it gains completed
    47	  days for days without articles inside its span (the fortnight has none: every day had articles) and nothing else.
    48	- The judge's request check (`watching`): a closed question is never in a round (production's selection), so no request names it.
    49	
    50	## 4. Prior decisions
    51	
    52	D54, D356 (pull mode freezes at the due day; no final review); D251 (day-start state); D12, D13, D31 (no wall clock; only pull
    53	mode acts on time, with its day passed in); D403 (an event's due day); D426 (the ladder step frozen; untouched); D427 (Step 2
    54	frozen; untouched). No decision bounds closing in the new system; the runner's guard was a stop written when closing was out of
    55	scope ("closing is pull mode's, not run here").
    56	
    57	## 5. Not covered, recorded
    58	
    59	Step 1's library does not learn that a question closed: it can still file a later fact only under that topic, which then has no
    60	home in the store (counted as dropped). Teaching Step 1 closings would change its input, a frozen piece (D387): not proposed here.
    61	
    62	## 6. Proof plan ($0)
    63	
    64	1. Tests in `test_ladder_adapter.py` on a fixture with one question due on a day with articles and one due on a day without:
    65	   frozen at the last answer, never-judged "no data to verify", the page before and after the due day, a link after closing dropped
    66	   and counted, the next day's round without the closed question; a mutant per rule (no closing; links written to closed
    67	   questions; days without articles skipped; the day completed at the sequence before the closing).
    68	2. The extension proof re-run: 19 of 19, every request and judgement unchanged.
    69	3. The decisive replay through the real loop: the extension proof's draw run on, with no further articles, to an end day past its
    70	   due days (2027-04-02): the six due questions closed on their own due days at their last answers, `v6` open, no model call, the
    71	   page before and after each due day.

**Keep the production fix as a candidate, but do not build the closing design as written.** The design misses a sequence collision that can put a later article on the wrong day, and its rule for dropping links is not production’s behaviour.

1. **The production fix addresses the stated defect.** On an empty day, `pull.closing_sequence` can create a new sequence for the closing. Completing that day at the preceding sequence leaves the closing outside the next day’s starting snapshot. Recomputing the last sequence after closing fixes that relationship. The new test exercises `replay.run` and checks the next-day snapshot, although it does not process a next-day article itself. [pull.py](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/src/hivemind/pull.py:19), [replay.py](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/src/hivemind/replay.py:119), [test](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/tests/test_closing_on_a_day_without_items.py:15)

   The parallel day runner is called **inside** `replay.run`, so the revised completion line applies to it too. Its manifest records a hash of all package Python files, however, so changing `replay.py` can cause an already-started parallel day to refuse resumption on runtime mismatch. That is a relevant failure state, not evidence that completed parallel days are wrong. [parallel_day.py](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/src/hivemind/parallel_day.py:38)

   I did not rerun the tests: this review is read-only, and the test writes temporary stores. The reported 12 passes and census remain the recorded results rather than independently reproduced results.

2. **The clean replay can reuse a closing’s sequence for a later article.** Its articles use the trace’s fixed article number `k` as their sequence. If an empty day closes a question, production’s closing function allocates the next sequence; the next article can then have that same `k`. The page maps a sequence to the *earliest* associated day, so later material can appear dated on the closing day. The proposed replay through 2027-04-02 has no later articles and would not catch this. [ladder_adapter.py](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/stage_b/ladder_adapter.py:318), [service.py](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/src/hivemind/service.py:30)

   The design needs one sequence owner or an explicit mapping from trace article numbers to store sequences, with every reader of those values accounted for. Prove it with an article, an empty due day, **and a later article**, checking the page and next request on each day.

3. **Dropping every link to a closed question is a new rule.** Production’s writer can link a revised statement to a closed question; it tests whether the question is open when deciding whether to queue a new judgement. `store.link` itself does not reject closed views. The design’s claim that production “never links one” therefore does not hold for all paths. Preserve or explicitly decide the intended history and later-link behaviour before implementing a blanket drop. [writing.py](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/src/hivemind/views/writing.py:259), [store.py](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/src/hivemind/views/store.py:349)

4. **The theme and guard rows need sharper contracts.** Closing a theme makes later requests omit it, but closing alone does not establish that its dependants are automatically judged. The guard’s invariant also needs cases for a question opened already overdue, an empty day, and a run starting or ending between article days. The proof should exercise these through the loop, including a never-judged question and later evidence, rather than only calling closing on a completed store. [CLOSING-DESIGN.md](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-run/CLOSING-DESIGN.md:18), [judging.py](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/src/hivemind/views/judging.py:76)

The next step is to revise the design around sequence ownership and the actual link and theme readers, then review and prove those paths at $0. The production change’s focused evidence is promising; its parallel-resumption consequence and required broader checks should be recorded before acceptance.

CONSENSUS: no, because the clean-loop design can collide sequences across days and introduces an unsupported closed-link rule.
